strengths: Addresses a well-motivated practical problem of fine-grained color control while preserving other visual attributes
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple baselines, models (SD3, FLUX.1-dev), and domains (images, videos, real images)
Extensive use of evaluation metrics including structure preservation (Y-GCS, Y-GMS) and editing quality measures beyond standard CLIP similarity
Good qualitative results demonstrating practical versatility including multi-object editing and integration with other editing models
Detailed ablation study (Table 4) showing contribution of each component
Reproducibility commitment with promised code release and detailed implementation details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (attention manipulation from prior work, structure preservation from Hertz et al. 2023, crude value-token copying for color preservation) without fundamental new insights

Technical soundness issue: attribute re-weighting method violates its own constraint that attention scores sum to 1, causing incorrect attention behavior that authors acknowledge but don't adequately resolve

Evaluation methodology concerns: heavy reliance on CLIP-based metrics with known limitations; user study is small-scale (24 participants, 34 cases) showing only 64.71% preference without statistical significance testing
Quantitative results not consistently superior: Table 1 shows competitors range 0.6180-0.7312 while method achieves 0.6473; Table 2 shows similar competitive but not dominant performance
Significant acknowledged limitations (Section B.10): fails to detect 'red trees', misinterprets 'lipstick' location, struggles with real image editing, performance limited by underlying model quality

Overclaimed contributions: abstract and conclusion claim 'solving fundamental problems' and achieving 'scalable, high-fidelity, controllable color editing' despite substantial acknowledged limitations and failure cases
Limited architectural generality: only tested on MM-DiT models; generalization to other diffusion architectures unclear
Ad-hoc design choices: mask threshold ε=0.1 appears arbitrary with minimal sensitivity analysis; many hyperparameter choices lack principled justification
Some baseline comparisons use author-created reimplementations rather than official versions, introducing potential bias despite authors' acknowledgment
Missing comparisons with recent color-specific editing methods; comparison mainly against general editing methods adapted for color

strengths: Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation with multiple baselines (training-free and commercial), diverse metrics beyond CLIP (structural preservation, edit quality), and a user study demonstrating 64.71% preference over baselines
Practical training-free method that generalizes across multiple state-of-the-art diffusion models (SD3, FLUX.1-dev, CogVideoX-2B) and modalities (images and videos) with convincing visual results
Well-motivated problem formulation with clear editing constraints (C1-C3) and a newly introduced ColorCtrl-Bench benchmark with 300 image pairs for community use

Technically sound three-component design integrating structure preservation (source/target branching), color preservation (vision-text mask extraction), and attribute re-weighting with clear ablation study demonstrating contribution of each component
Excellent presentation with detailed implementation details, specific hyperparameters for all baselines, reproducibility statements, proper ethics/consent documentation, and promise to release code
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: structure preservation directly adapts existing work (Cao et al., 2023), color preservation uses straightforward thresholding, and attribute re-weighting applies standard attention scaling; main contribution is combining these for MM-DiT, which is somewhat incremental

Evaluation concerns: CLIP similarity metrics are acknowledged as problematic (over-saturated edits in commercial models) yet remain primary metrics; user study with only 24 participants is modest; structural metrics rely on Canny edge maps and luminance-only gradients which may not capture all consistency issues

Mask extraction robustness issues: relies on fixed threshold τ=0.1 for vision-text similarity; failure cases (Fig. 16) show brittleness (red trees misidentified, upside-down bottle casing edited); limited analysis of mask extraction failure modes in complex scenes

Limited architectural analysis: claims MM-DiT enables 'precise attention-control editing strategies' but provides no concrete evidence comparing with U-Net models; architectural advantages asserted rather than demonstrated; attention mechanism differences from U-Net not deeply analyzed

Real image editing limitations: Section B.10 acknowledges significant challenges requiring carefully hand-tuned hyperparameters per model and dependence on inversion quality; this undermines practical applicability claims despite theoretical training-free benefit

Incomplete technical exploration: no investigation of perceptually-uniform color spaces (LAB, HSV) vs. RGB; no inference cost analysis; temporal coherence mechanisms for video not explained; limited evaluation metrics for video quality

Missing and incomplete baselines: instruction-based editing methods (e.g., InstructPix2Pix) only briefly compared; commercial baselines (FLUX.1, GPT-4o) are generative rather than editing-focused; limited exploration beyond SD3 and FLUX.1-dev

Benchmark clarity: distinction between ColorCtrl-Bench (300 pairs) and PIE-Bench (also used) unclear; public availability of ColorCtrl-Bench not specified; construction methodology for prompt pairs not detailed
